stem: Which of the following describes the typical timing of the growth spurt in girls compared to boys?

options.text: Girls have their growth spurt late in puberty, usually after menarche.
Girls have their growth spurt early in puberty, whereas boys have theirs in mid-to-late puberty.
Both genders peak simultaneously at approximately $12$ years of age.
Boys peak early to allow for muscle mass accumulation, while girls peak late.

explanation: Girls peak around age $11.5$, while boys wait until their testes are $10$ to $12\text{ ml}$ in volume, usually around age $13.5$.
rationale: Recall which gender finishes their primary height gain shortly after their first period.

optionExplanations.A: Growth velocity in girls typically peaks before menarche and slows down significantly afterward.
optionExplanations.B: Girls peak around age $11.5$, while boys wait until their testes are $10$ to $12\text{ ml}$ in volume, usually around age $13.5$.
optionExplanations.C: There is a distinct sexual dimorphism in the timing of the pubertal growth spurt, with girls peaking earlier.
optionExplanations.D: Muscle mass gain in boys is actually a late pubertal event, following the height spurt.

originalCorrectOptionTexts: Girls have their growth spurt early in puberty, whereas boys have theirs in mid-to-late puberty.
